saints.name: St. Hugh of Grenoble
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The reforming Bishop of Grenoble who welcomed St. Bruno and gave the Carthusians their first home…
biography: Born in 1053 at Châteauneuf-sur-Isère near Valence, Hugh was a canon of Valence while still a layman. Elected bishop of Grenoble at the Council of Avignon in 1080, he was conducted to Rome and ordained by Pope Gregory VII himself, and found his see ruined in morals and in goods.

For fifty-two years he laboured against simony and the laxity of his clergy, restoring discipline and recovering the patrimony of his church, long disputed by Count Guigues III of Albon until an accord in 1099. Once he sought to resign his see for the cloister of Cluny, but the pope ordered him back to his charge.

In 1084, after dreaming of seven stars, he welcomed Bruno of Cologne and six companions and gave them the wild Alpine valley of the Chartreuse, where the Carthusian Order began; Hugh remained its lifelong protector. He died on 1 April 1132 and was canonized only two years later by Innocent II.
saints.knownFor: Reforming his diocese and giving the Carthusians the valley of the Chartreuse.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 1 April
